title: Password: Password
story: IT is running its first ever password audit.
It is also IT's last ever password audit, if the results are what we think.
Somewhere in this company is an account that breaks EVERY rule in the policy.
Not most of them. All of them.
objective: Find the account whose password breaks every single rule in the policy.

/srv/audit/password_policy.txt: DEADPORT PASSWORD POLICY (v1, written on a napkin)
4. NOT contain the account's own username
Violators will be asked, gently, to stop.
/srv/audit/auditor_notes.txt: Why are the passwords stored in plaintext?
Bob says 'so we can audit them'.
I hate that this is technically correct.

hints: Check each account against all four rules. Write it down if you need to.
Several accounts break three rules. Only one breaks all four.
Count the characters carefully. 'ceopassword' is shorter than it looks.
completion: The CEO has been asked to change it.
The CEO has changed it to 'ceopassword2'. Progress.
